enumerate each modelled state field and assert its transition set is closed; the discriminating case is satisfy-then-unsatisfy on a non-test AC, which is the instance that produced the rule. **THE TEST COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT RESTATED HERE (dc 2026-08-30, on vc's ruling).** This clause said `11 tests GREEN at acf8491`; the file ran 22 when driven, and the clause was last read 2026-08-17 -- citation rot in this row's own evidence field. **Writing the new number in would mint a fresh copy on a fresh decay schedule**, so it is gone rather than updated. Drive the file to learn the count; the row is held at partial coverage on the AT-00.5 precedent, and what it needs is stated by BEHAVIOUR below. **THE SECOND-CONDITION ARM NOW EXISTS AND PASSES (cc, 2026-08-17): `the_wider_reading_fires_on_edgeless_rows_only` (renamed with `Unbuilt` -> `edgeless`; named here for findability, and the arm is identified by what it measures), and `Disposition::Unbuilt` carries `Entry` so how a value gets IN is declared beside what is unavailable.** The earlier note here said the arm was missing, and that is no longer the reason this row is red -- correcting it rather than leaving it, because a stale reason is what the next reader inherits. What the arm established is that measuring the debt is not paying it: all FOUR `Unbuilt` rows -- `Thread.acceptance`, `Criterion.kind`, `AcceptanceTest.kind`, `Issue.status`, four and not the five this note previously claimed -- hold values authored canon puts there with no verb to move them. **So the row is red for owed WORK, not for a missing measurement -- and as of 2026-08-17 that work is RULED AND UNBLOCKED rather than waiting on hv.** It was escalated as one ruling across all four rows, bundled with the self-loop question because both are one rule spanning several machines; **hv ratified both on vc's recommendation and the answer is materially smaller than the row implied.** Only `Issue.status` becomes a machine (Machine 4, declared from v2's measured behaviour, no guards). `Criterion.kind` folds into Machine 3 as a `(kind, state)` pair and `AcceptanceTest.kind` into the `AcceptanceTest.status` machine -- **neither is independently movable, because the kind/state pairing is enforced in the JSON Schema face (`model.rs:414-432`, `tests/ac_kind_state_invariant.rs`), so a conversion is one act moving two fields and is a transition of the PAIR rather than of either field.** `Thread.acceptance` is `Option<AcceptanceMode>`, an attribute rather than a lifecycle, and is **immutable after creation** -- owed nothing. **Self-loops are legal across all four machines, accepted-and-reported at exit 0 WITHOUT re-running the guard**, which is the half that matters here: re-running the gate on an already-`Completed` thread would let a criterion added after the close block a thread that is legitimately finished, which is this very criterion's own history. Full text in `data-model.md`. **What remains for this row is implementation and not adjudication**: wire Machine 4, accept self-loops on Machines 1-3, give each `kind` its paired conversion, and re-disposition `Thread.acceptance` off `Unbuilt`. **The row stays red until those land and the walk agrees with the ratified graph. CLOSING CONDITION SHARPENED 2026-08-17 (vc), on cc's finding, and it corrects MY OWN wording: "the walk" is singular and THREE tests carry that property between them, no one of them alone.** `the_transition_table_transcribes_the_ratified_machines_edge_for_edge` (cc's rename landed, and it is the honest name: it says `transcribes`, which is what it measures) compares the DECLARED table against `RATIFIED_*` consts transcribed from data-model.md -- **neither side is the implementation, so it is green with zero code driving any edge**, which cc observed empirically before adding Machine 4's drive arm. `every_declared_edge_is_a_mutation_that_exists` is what drives them, and `a_transition_the_ratified_machine_does_not_declare_is_refused` is what shuts the other door. **This row may not be closed on the first alone**, and its name is the reason someone would try: it says `implemented` and it measures `declared`. cc is renaming it; the rename does not change what any of the three measures, so this condition is stated by BEHAVIOUR and not by test name -- table matches ratified, every declared edge drives, every undeclared pair refuses. **FORM CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (vc), `to-write` -> `red`, note restored by hand after 0033. The struck clause said `red` "would be a false statement about a suite that passes", and that is the reading I corrected on 2026-08-15**: the AT's status is the CRITERION's state, not the file's, so a passing suite behind an unmet criterion is exactly what a red row plus this note is for -- while `to-write` claimed no file existed when one does, and kept L2/L3 switched off besides. **MACHINE 4 LANDED 2026-08-17 (cc, `b504d91b`) AND THE THREE WALKS MEASURED AGAINST IT -- the third is VACUOUS FOR THIS MACHINE, BY CONSTRUCTION, AND MY OWN CLOSING CONDITION CANNOT SEE THAT** (vc, at `e7cf7902`, 18/18 green). Walk 1 carries `("Issue", "status", RATIFIED_ISSUE)`, and since `declared()` panics on a non-`State` field, walk 1 passing is itself the proof that `Issue.status` is a `State` -- which puts it in walk 2's `all_fields()` sweep, where `execute()`'s `("Issue", "status")` arm drives both edges. Two of three, established rather than asserted. **The third exercises ZERO pairs: Machine 4 is TOTAL.** Two states and two edges, so for every (verb, state) pair the state is either in the verb's from-set or is the verb's own target, and the walk's filter (`!from.contains(s) && s != to`) admits neither. Computed from the transcribed table: `issues.close` NONE, `issues.open` NONE. **So "every undeclared pair refuses" is satisfied by there being no undeclared pair, which is a true statement and not a measurement** -- and the condition I wrote to stop this row closing on a vacuous green is, for this machine, met by one. The clause stands for Machines 1-3 unchanged; for Machine 4 the honest reading is that the property is discharged by the machine's shape rather than by a test, and the row must not be read as three walks agreeing when one of them never spoke. **AND THE ZERO IS CURRENTLY INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN OMISSION, BECAUSE `Issue` IS NOT IN WALK 3'S LIST AT ALL** (`:1301-1303` enumerates `Thread`, `WorkPackage`, `Criterion`). A walk that did not visit a machine and a walk that visited it and found nothing to refuse produce the same output -- none -- which is ic's harness rule arriving on this row's own closing condition. **TWO HAND-ENUMERATED LISTS OMIT MACHINE 4 AND BOTH OMISSIONS ARE FREE TODAY, WHICH IS THE WORST STATE FOR THEM: nothing will red when they stop being free.** Walk 3 (`:1301`) and `a_verb_declared_to_record_a_justification_refuses_a_blank_one` (`:1376`) both list three entities; `attempt()`'s `match entity` (`:1242`) has three arms and a `panic!` default. The justification omission costs nothing only because `RATIFIED_ISSUE` declares no guards -- **the day anyone gives `issues close` a reason, that check silently does not run.** **The doc comment at `:1366` narrates this exact incident on the previous machine** -- `Criterion` missing from the loop left `ac.withdraw`'s ratified `ReasonRecorded` "transcribed, conformance-checked, and dead" -- and closes _"the list is now derived from the ratified tables themselves"_. **That is true of the VERB axis and false of the ENTITY axis, and the incident it describes was an entity omission**, so the repair hardened the axis that was not the problem. Recommended to cc and not ruled: derive all three entity lists from one array so a fifth machine cannot land in walk 1 and be missed by the others, and record each machine's undeclared-pair count so a structural zero reads as a zero rather than as an absence. **BOTH BUILT AND MUTATION-PROVED 2026-08-17 (cc, `1721e4bb`) -- AND BINDING THE LIST TO THE CODE FOUND THAT THIS ROW'S CENTRAL CLAUSE HAD BEEN DISCHARGED OVER TWO THIRDS OF ITS POPULATION.** `transitions.rs` classifies **SIX** fields as `Disposition::State`; only **four** carried transcriptions. `AcceptanceTest.status` and `WorkPackage.scope` were in the code, driven by the drive-walk, closed by the closure-walk, **and compared to nothing** -- so _"the implemented graph must MATCH THE RATIFIED MACHINES EXACTLY"_ was green while a third of the machines had no ratified graph to match against. **The class one level above the one both of us were looking at: the walks agreed, and their subject was a subset of the machines.** Note what was NOT wrong: `data-model.md:487` already said _"Three machines are documented above; `transitions.rs` classifies FIVE fields"_ and named both undocumented ones. **The document was right and the instrument was short, and nothing compared the two lists** -- which is why cc's binding of `RATIFIED` to `transitions::FIELDS` is the fix and a longer hand-list would not have been. **CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (cc, and the correction strengthens the conclusion rather than softening it): the document says FIVE and cc measured SIX, and BOTH ARE RIGHT AT THEIR OWN REVISION.** `Issue.status` was `Disposition::Unbuilt` until Machine 4 landed at `b504d91b` **that same morning**, which made it the sixth. **So the document's count was accurate when written and cc's own commit staled it hours before cc measured against it** -- the tree variant with cc as the cause and the document as the victim. **It is the strongest argument available for the binding**: a hand-list would have gone short again the same day, by the hand of the node maintaining it, and a number written in prose is a dated measurement rather than a rule. **RULED (vc, provisional pending hv): `RATIFIED_WITHOUT_A_TABLE` CHECKS THE RATIFICATION, IT DOES NOT ALTER IT, and cc should not withdraw it as offered.** Four reasons, in order of weight. The sentences are quoted **verbatim** from `data-model.md:489-490` and are the ratified text. The assertions map one-to-one onto the sentence's clauses and add nothing -- _"one verb"_ is `verbs.len() == 1`, _"any value ->"_ is `edge.from.is_empty()`, _"-> any value"_ is targets covering every `initial` state. **Third and decisive: "it does not need a table" is a claim about the graph's SHAPE, and it is true only while the shape holds** -- asserted once, at authoring time, and never revisited since, which is precisely a standing assumption nothing reads back. **Fourth, the tell: every failure message names the remedy as _write the table_ rather than _fix the code_.** The test does not forbid a second verb; it forbids a second verb going unratified. That is a trigger, and a trigger on a dormant assumption is the opposite of altering it. **Also ruled: the two remain ratified WITHOUT tables** -- inventing transcriptions for graphs whose own ratification says they carry no information would manufacture exactly the second artefact this thread has spent the day counting. **AND cc's INDEPENDENT WALK-3 DEFECT IS THE BEST FINDING OF THE THREE**: the filter excluded a verb's target **per EDGE**, so `ac.rescope` from `computed` was required to refuse on the strength of the edge whose target is `unsatisfied`, while `computed` is the same verb's OTHER target. **The self-loop predicate is per-VERB and a kind-dependent verb's target is a SET**; testing one member at a time is a well-formed wrong answer. **And it was invisible for exactly as long as `ac_rescope` hand-checked its from-state and refused everything -- so 0053's defect is what kept the walk that should have caught 0053 green.** A defect masking its own detector, which is why the fix and the test had to land together


**PREDICATE ESTABLISHED 2026-08-30 (dc, on vc's ruling that it must be settled before the row moves): `mutation_completeness.rs` DOES compute the machine agreement, and the gate does not.** All three carriers live in the file this row cites and all three are green. **The pre-commit `machine-table` guard is a DIFFERENT artefact scoring a DIFFERENT population** -- it compares `data-model.md` against `transitions.rs`, ratified prose against its transcription, and NEITHER side is the service layer. So it can report `47 agree, 0 disagree` while nothing drives a single edge. That is the `AT-00.5` mechanism exactly, and it is why 22 green in the Rust test was not evidence until this was checked.

**AND THE ROW IS STILL RED FOR ONE NAMED, BOUNDED REASON.** Of the four items this note listed as remaining, three have landed: Machine 4 is wired, self-loops are accepted, and `Thread.acceptance` is off `edgeless`. **The `kind` paired conversions have not.** `Criterion.kind` and `AcceptanceTest.kind` are the two rows still `edgeless`, and each carries a note saying the conversion *"currently needs a hand-edit"* -- **which is the precise condition AC-04.6 exists to forbid**, in the same words as the `ac satisfy` instance hv ruled on. The residual work is two verbs, not a measurement.
